predecessor.rule: This is a genuinely new, literature-structured family; it is not a rescue by dropping failed statistical gates.

objective: Test whether source-language-specific Japanese fundamental/macro news adds incremental next-day volatility-state information for the Nikkei daily futures proxy.

evidence.paper: Lee A. Smales (2026), When news travels: The role of sentiment in CME Nikkei futures returns
evidence.implication: Separate Japanese-related fundamental sentiment by source language; Japanese- and English-language information can matter differently across regimes.

evidence.paper: Feng, Fu & Shi (2022), How does news sentiment affect the states of Japanese stock return volatility?
evidence.implication: News occurrence/sentiment, especially macroeconomic news, is a volatility-state candidate.

source.interpretation: sourcelang restricts the original publication language while keyword matching uses GDELT's English machine translations.
source.acquisition: Quarter-sized windows from the outset; single connection; paced requests; cumulative Actions cache; bounded adaptive split only on a failing quarter.
source.raw_storage: Actions cache only; durable repository output contains derived features/results/provenance, not article bodies.

acquisition_budget.resume_rule: A resume may only reuse cumulative cache and fetch missing chunks. Queries, dates, features, statistical models and thresholds may not change.
acquisition_budget.terminal_rule: If the complete four-cell panel cannot be acquired after three bounded runs, classify G1 as DATA_INCONCLUSIVE.
acquisition_budget.logical_attempt_rule: Runs triggered by both push and pull_request from the identical request commit SHA are one logical acquisition attempt; this control-plane duplication does not create a new hypothesis/trial.

attempt_1.note: Future resumes use PR-only triggering and cumulative cache.

attempt_2.cache_policy: Reuse latest cache from research/news-language-source-g1 and fetch only missing chunks.

JAPAN_MACRO_JA.query: ("Bank of Japan" OR "Japan inflation" OR "Japanese wages" OR "Japan monetary policy") sourcelang:japanese

JAPAN_MACRO_EN.query: ("Bank of Japan" OR "Japan inflation" OR "Japanese wages" OR "Japan monetary policy") sourcelang:english

JAPAN_EQUITY_JA.query: ("Nikkei 225" OR "Japanese stocks" OR "Tokyo stock market") sourcelang:japanese

JAPAN_EQUITY_EN.query: ("Nikkei 225" OR "Japanese stocks" OR "Tokyo stock market") sourcelang:english

timing.predictor_alignment: Strict prior-day as-of only; exact same-day match is excluded.
timing.target: Next-day squared Nikkei futures-index proxy return.
timing.note: G1 is daily language/source conditioning, not an intraday session test.

forbidden: Drop Japanese or English cells because they underperform
Merge languages only after observing results
Add US-tech/Fed/FX/geopolitical categories to this G1 family
Turn a volatility-state pass into directional trading without a new preregistration
Claim source-language filtering reproduces proprietary TRNA sentiment analytics
formal_jnu_promotion: Requires subsequent confirmation with true JNU/OSE data if used for intraday session decisions.

data_integrity_revision.trigger: Cache audit found at least one omitted calendar date (2023-03-23) in a successful GDELT TimelineTone chunk; external narrow-query verification was unavailable.
rule: Reindex every source cell to an explicit calendar-day grid.
Any date omitted by GDELT is NaN, not zero and not forward-filled.
Derived abs_tone and tone_ewm are also unavailable on a missing source date.
All four cells and the baseline use one common causal availability mask for training and OOS comparison.
This revision changes no keyword query, source language, target, date range, half-life, OOS start, recent window, bootstrap, Holm alpha or pass threshold.

quality_gate.rationale: A four-cell comparison is not interpretable if source omissions materially change the evaluation population; coverage is a data-quality gate, not a performance threshold.
quality_gate.no_rescue: Do not drop a low-coverage cell after inspection to raise common coverage.
